name: Shannon Singleton

bio.statement: Singleton currently serves as Multnomah County's District 2 Commissioner.
In her voters' pamphlet statement, Singleton lists her occupational background as housing policy director, executive director of JOIN, and social worker.
bio.excerpt: Housing Policy Director, Executive Director, JOIN, Social Worker

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

bio.statement: Singleton's pamphlet statement lists bachelor's and master's degrees in social work.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

bio.statement: Singleton's pamphlet statement lists prior service on A Home for Everyone Coordinating Board, the Portland Housing Advisory Commission and the Metro Housing Bond Oversight Committee.
bio.excerpt: A Home for Everyone Coordinating Board, Portland Housing Advisory Commission, Metro Housing Bond Oversight Committee

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

bio.statement: Her county profile says Singleton served as housing policy advisor to Governor Kate Brown starting in 2019.
bio.excerpt: In 2019 Shannon joined Governor Kate Brown's administration as her housing policy advisor.

positions.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Singleton says her approach will find lasting solutions to the homelessness crisis, lower costs and support families.
positions.excerpt: That's how we find real, lasting solutions to our homelessness crisis, lower costs, and support families.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

verification.note: Statement added 'draw in people closest to problems', which is not in the excerpt (that content is item p2). Reworded to match the excerpt only.

positions.statement: In her pamphlet statement, Singleton says she will build better systems by involving people closest to the problem.
positions.excerpt: I'll build better systems by drawing in people closest to the problem

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: Singleton's campaign site says she aims to improve service delivery in housing, addiction, behavioral health and public safety.
positions.excerpt: ensure better service delivery in housing, addiction, behavioral health, and public safety.

positions.statement: Singleton's campaign site says she wants to connect hundreds of workers to union jobs through apprenticeships and skills training.
positions.excerpt: connect hundreds of workers to good-paying union jobs through apprenticeships and skills training.

positions.statement: Singleton's campaign site says she wants to make Multnomah County a good place to own and run a business.
positions.excerpt: make Multnomah County a great place to own and run a business.

positions.statement: Willamette Week reported in February 2026 that Singleton has been vocal about getting people arrested for possession through the county's deflection program.
positions.excerpt: Singleton has been particularly vocal about getting people arrested for possession through the deflection program

verification.note: Excerpt says 'possession', not 'drug possession'; removed the added word. Excerpt confirmed on page (sentence continues 'and into housing').

positions.statement: Willamette Week reported that Singleton highlighted her work with Brim-Edwards on stricter rules for lobbyists.
positions.excerpt: Singleton highlighted her work, alongside Brim-Edwards, to create more stringent rules for lobbyists

positions.statement: In a February 2026 OPB report, Singleton said she wants to serve where she can make the most change.
positions.excerpt: "I want to serve where I can make the most change," Singleton said in a press release.
